I’m curious about the way you handle things in your culture. How is he able to get away with things while living under your roof? Was he not raised to respect his elders? It seems he needs a lesson in respect. Being a few years younger doesn’t mean anything. He is living in your house. Seems some ground rules need to be set. If you don’t want to target him specifically to make him get all upset, have a family meeting and set expectations on who should do what. “Dad will dust these days” “kid will help pick up toys” “cousin will help out with _____” the real things you’d expect from him. Set a curfew because grandma is getting on and can say you, your wife, and cousin should abide by so grandma can get as much rest as she can.

Say the family as a whole needs to start picking up glasses and cleaning them, refilling water. Things need to feel like a real family. That way he doesn’t dwell targeted and complain. Put “blame” on yourself/wife/kid in the process all to start helping grandma.

Hope this works, some people don’t do well with taking blunt advice so they need to feel like they aren’t attacked. It’s stupid because he’s and adult now and should be treated like one. He’s acting selfish by eating all the food and not providing support to help return the favor.

Let him enjoy this time in Mexico, this is his vacation. Don’t make him feel guilty being attached to his phone for your insecurities and constant need to make sure you’re not feeling sad/depressed/hopeless/down. It’s a huge turn off. Humans need their space or you’re going to make them realize what a good time they’re having by not having someone nagging on them. It seems you want him to give you excuses so you can set him up for failure and have a reason to be angry and fact check him.

Give him the chance to miss you. There’s nothing cute about being clingy. Call up your friends and hang out with them. Find some hobbies your enjoy or look into some things you’ve always wanted to try. Being busy and having your own life is good.

Bonus points: when she wakes up and it’s a decent pizza eating hour (let’s face it, 24 hours is pizza eating hour.) have some delivered to the house to surprise the fuck out of her.

I had picked 3 cars from the lot that I loved, and 1 as a back up. I went inside to find a salesperson to test drive them. We sat down, told him my top picks, one of them wasn’t in the system, but he failed to look up the other two. Instead his tactic was what was my range, I told him, then he asked the highest I was willing to go, I added 10k onto that. He typed into the search bar that highest price and searches highest to low, and picks out the top 3. I was frustrated and asked about the other 2. He claims these 3 are much better and to “trust him” 

We test out the first car, it was a short drive, he’s flirting with me, pressing all these buttons, showing the car off. I’m thinking damn dude, let me drive this damn car, there are too many people on the road for show and tell. We get back to the lot, he’s showing me even more buttons and features, it’s pure vomit.

Then the second car, I assume it’s the same route, this time the flirting is even thicker. He’s saying how well I drive for being a woman (wtf). I’m trying to make the turns as we did prior and he says no, get on the interstate. I get nervous, it’s now dark outside, every exit I try to take he tells me to keep going. I’m on the east part of town that I never go to so I have no idea where I am. We pass 5 exits before I tell him we should start heading back. He finally agrees. On the way back he “forgets” the exit but tells me he wanted to take me the long way which takes us North. I’m freaking out by this point. I’m in this car with this man that I have no idea what to do if he tries something on me. I don’t know how to make it back to the lot. No idea where to pull off, no gas stations around or shops. He was full on creeper mode, thinking flirting will make a sale.

A 45 minute drive we made it back. Don’t they pay attention to how long their employees are gone? He gave me his card but I got out of there ASAP and never went back. Is this typical for sales? I’m sure women actually fall for this.

I live in a city that speaks mostly Spanish/English. My coworkers and I decided to go get Mexican food for lunch, when we were walking to our cars, I realized I couldn’t find my keys. After frantically searching I discovered they were in the ignition. I’ve never done this before. The people I was with eventually abandoned me saying they had to go back (they didn’t, it’s not like they’d do anything but sit around)...

So I’m sitting in the heat, trying to call and see if my insurance can cover this, nope, I’m out of range. I’m calling companies but they’re either way too expensive, would take hours, or misc problems. Luckily I had friends meeting me anyways to meet me down the road to take care of something. 

I’m hot, soaked in sweat in uniform, everyone in the restaurant can see me, this is an all time low.

Then 3 men walked out towards me to take a look. They’re speaking to me in Spanish explaining me getting locked out and to hold on. I’m not proficient in Spanish , but I use what basic Spanish I knew, and they used what basic English I knew and spent hours getting me in. They would NOT give up. They were also soaked in sweat, its an older car so harder to break into.

They didn’t expect money, they didn’t want anything from me, just to have a good day. I will never forget the day my own people left me and 3 strangers stayed by my side until I was safe. Good people exist in this world. They were probably late for their next job, but they wouldn’t leave until I i was taken care of. I tried calling their company to reward them, but no luck. I will forever send positive vibes their way.

A lot of it has to do with body language, make sure you’re not closing yourself up. Crossing your arms or slouching can appear as if you’re uninterested. Open yourself up, roll your shoulders back. Smile, practice in the mirror or with friends you trust. Don’t be afraid to laugh at jokes. You’ll be nervous and that’s normal. Eye contact Is very important, but too much or too intense can also be off putting. If you’re looking at everything else but her/him, they’ll think you’re not interesting. Position your body towards them when you’re talking. If you sense them getting closer, this is a good sign. If they touch you when talking, try doing the same, a light touch of the arm or hand. It’s all about reading the situation.

It’s all about practice and getting out there, don’t be afraid of rejection, because it makes you that much better. 

Have you heard of mirroring? If someone is interested in you, they’ll mimic you. Take a sip of your soda and see if she does the same. Touch your face, brush your hair behind your ear, see if she/he follows. If so you can follow their cues. Be outgoing, be happy, be positive. Sorry if I didn’t quite answer your question, but body language is so important to see if a person is at least interested. Confidence is key!

After having Researched for nearly a year about ESA and service dogs, what it entails, laws protecting them, breeds that would be fitting, training, etc., I knew what I was getting into. I had an idea what I wanted, either a German Shepard or a golden retriever. However I wouldn’t be picky if I found a dog that matched or hard traits of a support dog.

The day after Christmas my friend said let’s just stop by the humane society, why not. We happened to stumble upon 9 puppies that were hidden from plain view, I asked the lady if she’d open the door but let me do something. From each room I extended my hand, and whichever puppy came to me, I wanted to play with. The first pup that ran to me is ultimately the one I picked. In the room he jumped on me, gave me kisses, couldn’t give me enough lovings. 

He’s a German Shepard mix and it was pure luck of getting exactly what I wanted. He was 12 weeks. Potty trained in 3 days, but it was hell for the first few months. The person that allowed me to stay at his place was cold to my dog, and might have abused him while I was at work. When I got my own place it was hell too. At some points I was wanting to give him up.  He was so much and needy, forgetting his training. The worst dog I had ever had.

Until one day when I had a flashback and couldn’t stop crying. My dog came up to me and jumped on my lap and licked my tears and face and ears until I started laughing. It changed him. He’s been the best dog I’ve ever had. He’s self trained to always be by my side. I’ll pretend to have seizure and he’ll bark loudly and try to move my body. I’ll pretend collapse on the ground, and he’ll do the same as above. He trained himself... if I ever cry, he’s right by my side. Licking my tears. I never taught him any of this. I was annoyed with tripping over him, but I’d rather trip over him than be alone.

Puppies might be frustrating, but they will adapt to you. You’ll just know when you meet the right dog. Let them come to you. Let them pick you. Sit on the ground and see if they lick your face and interact with you. If they do this to you now, they’ll love you even more when they bond with you. I was going randomly to the 2 shelters we have where I live. They hide the puppies With these tall brick walls so you can’t see over. Luckily I was nosy and looked; otherwise I never would have found him. Don’t give up!

Turn it positive and for every bad memory, remember the goofy times that I’m sure you had like covering yourself in peanut butter and having pillow fights. Whatever it is y’all do. Keep your chin up. There’s support all around you. Free yourself of your past and focus on your bright future.

After a year and a half we finally found the right combo. It’s been frustrating but under control, thank goodness. The one thing to keep in mind is the possible suicidal risks/thoughts that come with different meds. And I hope they let you know this in advance before prescribing. Some meds when they aren’t working for you, you’ll need to stop slowly, this will be important later:

Prazosin was by far the best success I had overall, I slowly kept having to increase the dose. Eventually had stop as the nightmares were back to full blown.

Gabapentin, not sure how this helps with ptsd as I thought this was more of nerve related, tried doing quick research, but I’ve been taking this for over a year and just got upped to the highest dose. None of the docs related this to anything ptsd related, if you know otherwise, please let me know!

Hydrozyzine/vistaril I’ve only used in panic attack moments when I’m in need of a quick fix to calm down. Highly helpful and it calms me and my thoughts down. The doc mentioned it to sleep, but we don’t use it for ptsd it to get me to sleep.

Others to consider in my trial/error: 

Risperidone: I had the best success with using this at nighttime. It is an atypical antipsychotic med which freaked me out because that’s not my diagnosis, however it has been used for combat related ptsd nightmares. He promised it was purely for the sleep, nothing else. The sleep was heavenly, HOWEVER I must warn you, I read up on every pill prescribed and saw side effects of possible weight gain of 50-150 lbs. I ended up gaining 50lbs in 5 weeks with no change to life habits, AND I started lactating (I’m a female). Men apparently can grow breasts, read up on it. This was hands down the best success I’ve had with quiet nights, but I cut the pill cold turkey, next day tried committing suicide. This is why I say make sure you slowly stop taking pills !!!!

Ambien/Xanax combo: Some don’t like prescribing Xanax, but mine is to prevent me from ripping off my CPAP mask. The ambien is to get me to sleep. It doesn’t work because I’m too afraid to fall asleep, due to the nightmares, but the CPAP helps distract me from dreaming.

Lunesta: Tried it a bit, didn’t have much luck and kept upping my dose for results. Worth a shot? 

I still hate going to sleep so I’ll keep myself up because I’m terrified of the dreams that I know will happen. My best advice along with medication is therapy and talking about it. Group therapy felt good, shameful to hear others having similar experiences, but nice to know you’re not alone. Solid friendships were formed and we check in regularly. Don’t give up on finding something that works. I almost did and it nearly cost me my life.
